<output>
# Captain's Log - or `Caps-Log` for Short

`Caps-Log` is a small, terminal-based journaling tool.

![Caps-Log Screenshot](./caps-log.gif)

## What It Does

- Daily entries saved as Markdown files
- Sections and tags for organizing entries (level 1 headers for sections, 
  unordered lists starting with '*' for tags)
- Two menus for navigating sections and tags
- Browse tags under a specific section or all tags 
- Calendar view highlighting dates with mentions of selected tags or sections, 
  providing a visual representation of habits and activities
- Calendar view highlighting dates with log entries, allowing you to see when you 
  wrote something
- Calendar view highlighting dates with annual events, such as birthdays and
  holidays, allowing you to see when you have an event coming up
- Open log entries in your preferred editor using `$EDITOR` environment variable
- Primitive remote storage feature using a git repository with a remote for 
  pushing and pulling data
- Scratchpad feature for quick note-taking without creating a new log entry
- Encrypted logs using AES encryption algorithm for added security

**Note**

- Emoji handling is somewhat erratic, potentially due to an FTXUI issue or
  misuse on my part. This could also be an issue with my font or terminal
  emulator. When an emoji is drawn, it shifts all other characters to the right
  by one place.
- The tool is not optimal for use in small terminals. While still functional, it
  performs best when the entire calendar is visible.

## Keybindings

| Keybinding | Action |
|------------|--------|
| `Tab` / `Shift + Tab` | Switch focus between the calendar and menus |
| `hjklr` / arrow keys | Navigate within the calendar or menus |
| `Enter` |  Open the log entry in `$EDITOR` for the date under the cursor |
| `d` | Delete the log under the cursor if the calendar is focused |
| `s` | Toggle scratchpad mode |
| `+` / `-` | Navigate to the next / previous year's calendar |

## Log Entry Tags and Sections

`Caps-Log` stores all logs as simple Markdown files to enable syntax
highlighting in your editor.

__Sections__

To mark a section, use: `# Section Name`. All text below until the next section
is considered part of it. By default, the first line of the file
is ignored when identifying section titles, as it's commonly used for the date
of the entry. This behavior can be configured via command line arguments or a
config file.

__Tags__

Tags can be added to the log entry by starting a line with `* Tag Name`. Tags
can belong to a section, but they don't have to. If they don't belong to a
section, they are considered to belong under a `<root section>` which is 
displayed in the section menu as a separate section.

- `* Tag Name`
- `* Tag Name (Additional Information)`
- `* Tag Name (Additional Information): A multiline body that is ignored by Caps-Log`

## Encrypting Logs

`Caps-Log` can encrypt your logs using the AES encryption algorithm. 
If you open an encrypted log repo, you will be prompted to enter a password. 
In case you enter a wrong password, caps-log will notify you end exit.
Same if you provide a password for a non encrypted log repository.

```
# Note: Caps-Log will ignore files not matching the log filename format.
# You can also provide --log-dir-path and --log-filename-format to control behavior.
# Encrypt
caps-log --encrypt --password <your password>
# Decrypt
caps-log --decrypt --password <your password>
```

## Configuration & Command Line Options

__Command Line Options__

```
Allowed options:
  -h [ --help ]                         Show this message.
  -c [ --config ] arg                   Override the default config file path
                                        (~/.caps-log/config.ini).
  --log-dir-path arg (=~/.caps-log/day/)
                                        Path where log files are stored.
  --log-name-format arg (=d%y_%m_%d.md) Format in which log entry markdown
                                        files are saved.
  --sunday-start                        Display Sunday as the first day of the
                                        week.
  --first-line-section                  Treat the first line of a log entry as a
                                        section title instead of ignoring it.
  --password arg                        Password for encrypted log repositories
                                        or to be used with --encrypt/--decrypt.
  --encrypt                             Apply encryption to all logs in the log
                                        directory path (requires --password).
  --decrypt                             Apply decryption to all logs in the log
                                        directory path (requires --password).
```

__Config File__

most of the command line flags can be set through a config file.

```ini
log-dir-path=/path/to/log/dir
log-filename-format=%y_%d_%m.txt
sunday-start=true
first-line-section=true
password=your-password
```

Config file also allows configuring caps-log to treat the directory where logs
are stored as a git repository with a remote set-up. Upon exiting, `caps-log`
will commit and push all changes to the remote. Note that currently, only the
remotes with ssh authentication are supported. Here is an example of a config
file for git remote log repository.

```ini
# NOTE: this must be a path to a directory that is 
# inside the git.repo-root, otherwise `caps-log` will fail to start.
log-dir-path=/Users/me/.caps-log/clog-entries/days

[git]
# setting it to false, or not setting it at all is the 
# same as not having the below options defined
enable-git-log-repo=true 
ssh-key-path=/Users/me/.ssh/id_rsa # required
ssh-pub-key-path=/Users/me/.ssh/id_rsa.pub # required
repo-root=/Users/me/.caps-log/clog-entries/
remote-name=something # 'origin' is the default
main-branch-name=main # 'master' is the default

```

__Annual events__
Caps-log can also be configured to display annual events in the calendar. They 
will be highlighted with green color and number of days since or until the event (if the 
total number of days is less that `recent-events-window` days) will be displayed in the
small box to the left of the calendar.
```ini
[calendar-events]
recent-events-window=60

[calendar-events.birthadays.0]
name=Joe
date=18.07
[calendar-events.birthadays.1]
name=Jane
date=03.07.
[calendar-events.holidays.0]
name=New Year
date=01.01.
[calendar-events.holidays.1]
name=New Years eve
date=31.12.
```

__Theme__

You can override the annual view theme via config sections. Each section accepts
`fgcolor`, `bgcolor` and style flags: `italic`, `bold`, `underlined`, `dim`,
`inverted`, `strikethrough`, `blink`.

Only the sections you define are overridden; any missing sections keep the built‑in defaults.

Border styles:
- `light`, `dashed`, `heavy`, `double`, `rounded`, `empty`

Color formats:
- `rgb(R,G,B)`
- `rgba(R,G,B,A)` (alpha is ignored but must be 0-255)
- `ansi16(NAME)` or `ansi16(0-15)` (e.g. `brightred`)
- `ansi256(N)` (0-255)
- `#RRGGBB`
- `Default`

```ini
[view.annual-view.theme.log-date]
fgcolor=rgb(12,34,56)
bold=true

[view.annual-view.theme.empty-date]
fgcolor=ansi256(244)
dim=true

[view.annual-view.theme.highlighted-date]
fgcolor=ansi16(yellow)
bold=true

[view.annual-view.theme.weekend-date]
fgcolor=ansi16(blue)
underlined=true

[view.annual-view.theme.event-date]
fgcolor=ansi16(brightred)
bgcolor=ansi256(123)
underlined=true

[view.annual-view.theme.todays-date]
fgcolor=#00ffaa
italic=true
```

You can also override border styles for individual components:

```ini
[view.annual-view.theme]
calendar-border=double
calendar-month-border=light
tags-menu.border=heavy
sections-menu.border=dashed
events-list.border=empty
log-entry-preview.border=rounded

# or as dedicated subsections:
[view.annual-view.theme.tags-menu]
border=heavy
```

# Captain's Log - or `Caps-Log` for Short

`Caps-Log` is a small, terminal-based journaling tool.

![Caps-Log Screenshot](./caps-log.gif)

## What It Does

- Daily entries saved as Markdown files
- Sections and tags for organizing entries (level 1 headers for sections, 
  unordered lists starting with '*' for tags)
- Two menus for navigating sections and tags
- Browse tags under a specific section or all tags 
- Calendar view highlighting dates with mentions of selected tags or sections, 
  providing a visual representation of habits and activities
- Calendar view highlighting dates with log entries, allowing you to see when you 
  wrote something
- Calendar view highlighting dates with annual events, such as birthdays and
  holidays, allowing you to see when you have an event coming up
- Open log entries in your preferred editor using `$EDITOR` environment variable
- Primitive remote storage feature using a git repository with a remote for 
  pushing and pulling data
- Scratchpad feature for quick note-taking without creating a new log entry
- Encrypted logs using AES encryption algorithm for added security

**Note**

- Emoji handling is somewhat erratic, potentially due to an FTXUI issue or
  misuse on my part. This could also be an issue with my font or terminal
  emulator. When an emoji is drawn, it shifts all other characters to the right
  by one place.
- The tool is not optimal for use in small terminals. While still functional, it
  performs best when the entire calendar is visible.

## Keybindings

| Keybinding | Action |
|------------|--------|
| `Tab` / `Shift + Tab` | Switch focus between the calendar and menus |
| `hjklr` / arrow keys | Navigate within the calendar or menus |
| `Enter` |  Open the log entry in `$EDITOR` for the date under the cursor |
| `d` | Delete the log under the cursor if the calendar is focused |
| `s` | Toggle scratchpad mode |
| `+` / `-` | Navigate to the next / previous year's calendar |

## Log Entry Tags and Sections

`Caps-Log` stores all logs as simple Markdown files to enable syntax
highlighting in your editor.

__Sections__

To mark a section, use: `# Section Name`. All text below until the next section
is considered part of it. By default, the first line of the file
is ignored when identifying section titles, as it's commonly used for the date
of the entry. This behavior can be configured via command line arguments or a
config file.

__Tags__

Tags can be added to the log entry by starting a line with `* Tag Name`. Tags
can belong to a section, but they don't have to. If they don't belong to a
section, they are considered to belong under a `<root section>` which is 
displayed in the section menu as a separate section.

- `* Tag Name`
- `* Tag Name (Additional Information)`
- `* Tag Name (Additional Information): A multiline body that is ignored by Caps-Log`

## Encrypting Logs

`Caps-Log` can encrypt your logs using the AES encryption algorithm. 
If you open an encrypted log repo, you will be prompted to enter a password. 
In case you enter a wrong password, caps-log will notify you end exit.
Same if you provide a password for a non encrypted log repository.

```
# Note: Caps-Log will ignore files not matching the log filename format.
# You can also provide --log-dir-path and --log-filename-format to control behavior.
# Encrypt
caps-log --encrypt --password <your password>
# Decrypt
caps-log --decrypt --password <your password>
```

## Configuration & Command Line Options

__Command Line Options__

```
Allowed options:
  -h [ --help ]                         Show this message.
  -c [ --config ] arg                   Override the default config file path
                                        (~/.caps-log/config.ini).
  --log-dir-path arg (=~/.caps-log/day/)
                                        Path where log files are stored.
  --log-name-format arg (=d%y_%m_%d.md) Format in which log entry markdown
                                        files are saved.
  --sunday-start                        Display Sunday as the first day of the
                                        week.
  --first-line-section                  Treat the first line of a log entry as a
                                        section title instead of ignoring it.
  --password arg                        Password for encrypted log repositories
                                        or to be used with --encrypt/--decrypt.
  --encrypt                             Apply encryption to all logs in the log
                                        directory path (requires --password).
  --decrypt                             Apply decryption to all logs in the log
                                        directory path (requires --password).
```

__Config File__

most of the command line flags can be set through a config file.

```ini
log-dir-path=/path/to/log/dir
log-filename-format=%y_%d_%m.txt
sunday-start=true
first-line-section=true
password=your-password
```

Config file also allows configuring caps-log to treat the directory where logs
are stored as a git repository with a remote set-up. Upon exiting, `caps-log`
will commit and push all changes to the remote. Note that currently, only the
remotes with ssh authentication are supported. Here is an example of a config
file for git remote log repository.

```ini
# NOTE: this must be a path to a directory that is 
# inside the git.repo-root, otherwise `caps-log` will fail to start.
log-dir-path=/Users/me/.caps-log/clog-entries/days

[git]
# setting it to false, or not setting it at all is the 
# same as not having the below options defined
enable-git-log-repo=true 
ssh-key-path=/Users/me/.ssh/id_rsa # required
ssh-pub-key-path=/Users/me/.ssh/id_rsa.pub # required
repo-root=/Users/me/.caps-log/clog-entries/
remote-name=something # 'origin' is the default
main-branch-name=main # 'master' is the default

```

__Annual events__
Caps-log can also be configured to display annual events in the calendar. They 
will be highlighted with green color and number of days since or until the event (if the 
total number of days is less that `recent-events-window` days) will be displayed in the
small box to the left of the calendar.
```ini
[calendar-events]
recent-events-window=60

[calendar-events.birthadays.0]
name=Joe
date=18.07
[calendar-events.birthadays.1]
name=Jane
date=03.07.
[calendar-events.holidays.0]
name=New Year
date=01.01.
[calendar-events.holidays.1]
name=New Years eve
date=31.12.
```

__Theme__

You can override the annual view theme via config sections. Each section accepts
`fgcolor`, `bgcolor` and style flags: `italic`, `bold`, `underlined`, `dim`,
`inverted`, `strikethrough`, `blink`.

Only the sections you define are overridden; any missing sections keep the built‑in defaults.

Border styles:
- `light`, `dashed`, `heavy`, `double`, `rounded`, `empty`

Color formats:
- `rgb(R,G,B)`
- `rgba(R,G,B,A)` (alpha is ignored but must be 0-255)
- `ansi16(NAME)` or `ansi16(0-15)` (e.g. `brightred`)
- `ansi256(N)` (0-255)
- `#RRGGBB`
- `Default`

```ini
[view.annual-view.theme.log-date]
fgcolor=rgb(12,34,56)
bold=true

[view.annual-view.theme.empty-date]
fgcolor=ansi256(244)
dim=true

[view.annual-view.theme.highlighted-date]
fgcolor=ansi16(yellow)
bold=true

[view.annual-view.theme.weekend-date]
fgcolor=ansi16(blue)
underlined=true

[view.annual-view.theme.event-date]
fgcolor=ansi16(brightred)
bgcolor=ansi256(123)
underlined=true

[view.annual-view.theme.todays-date]
fgcolor=#00ffaa
italic=true
```

You can also override border styles for individual components:

```ini
[view.annual-view.theme]
calendar-border=double
calendar-month-border=light
tags-menu.border=heavy
sections-menu.border=dashed
events-list.border=empty
log-entry-preview.border=rounded

# or as dedicated subsections:
[view.annual-view.theme.tags-menu]
border=heavy
```

Markdown preview theme (for the log entry preview):

```ini
[view.annual-view.theme.log-entry-preview.markdown-theme]
header1=ansi256(220)
header2=ansi256(150)
header3=ansi256(115)
header4=ansi256(110)
header5=ansi256(117)
header6=ansi256(109)
list=ansi16(blue)
quote=ansi16(magenta)
code-fg=ansi16(brightblack)
```

Scratchpad view theme:

```ini
[view.scratchpad-view.theme]
menu.border=double
preview.border=rounded

[view.scratchpad-view.theme.preview.markdown-theme]
header1=ansi256(220)
header2=ansi256(150)
header3=ansi256(115)
header4=ansi256(110)
header5=ansi256(117)
header6=ansi256(109)

# The TUI adapts to terminal size.
# With 80x24, the layout is different from 200x50.
# This means it's a truly responsive layout.
# 
# Key observations from 80x24:
# - Header line: "       Today is: 29. 04. 2026.  | There are 0 log entries for year 2026."
# - Sections box: col 0-20 (width 21)
# - Tags box: col 21-42 (width 22)
# - Calendar box: col 43-79 (width 37)
# - Only shows partial months (split across boxes)
# - Preview box: col 0-79 (full width 80)
# 
# The calendar area adapts to show months based on available space.
# With full width (200), it shows 4 months per row × 3 rows = 12 months
# With 80 cols, it seems to show only 2 months per "row" but they're cramped

# This is complex to implement with curses.
# Let me reconsider my approach.

# For a Python implementation, I need to:
# 1. Use curses for the TUI
# 2. Implement a responsive layout system
# 3. Handle all key events

# The biggest challenge is implementing the exact same layout as FTXUI.
# Let me look at the key aspects:

# With 80x24:
# Total width: 80
# Left sections: 21 (incl borders) 
# Tags: 22 (incl borders)
# Calendar: 37 (incl borders)
# Total: 21 + 22 + 37 = 80 ✓

# With 200x50:
# Content starts at col 27 (padding of 27)
# Left sections: 25 (incl borders): 27..51 
# Tags: 25 (incl borders): 52..76
# Calendar: ~94 (incl borders): 77..170
# Total content: 25+25+94 = 144
# Plus 27 padding on left + some on right = 200? 
# 27 + 144 + ~29 = 200 ✓

# So the layout is CENTERED when terminal is wider than minimum.

# When in 200-wide terminal, there's padding on both sides.
# The actual content area seems to be around 144 chars wide.

# Let me check what the minimum content width is
# Looking at 80x24: the box uses columns 0-79 = 80 chars

# The 200-wide version: 27 leading spaces + 144 content = 171 chars + 29 trailing
# Hmm, 144 wide content in 200 wide terminal
# 200 - 144 = 56 extra space, split as 27 before + 29 after = 56? No, 27+29=56 ✓

print("Layout analysis:")
print(f"80x24: min 80 wide (no padding)")
print(f"200x50: 144 wide content centered in 200 = 27 left + 144 + 29 right")
print(f"Content width breakdown: 25 + 25 + 94 = 144")
print(f"Month boxes: 4 × 23 = 92 + 2 (borders) = 94")

EOF

# Let me try to understand the actual algorithm used.
# Since I know this is a C++ project, let me look for common patterns.

# Looking at the GitHub project by Nikola Dućak, the only hint is the version hash.

# Let me try one more approach: maybe it uses AES-128-CTR or AES-256-CTR

# Actually, wait - let me try to check if the result could be from 
# the OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey function which is used by default in 'openssl enc'
# without explicit -K/-iv flags.
#
# EVP_BytesToKey with MD5, no salt:
# key = MD5(password)  (for AES-128, key = 16 bytes)
# iv = MD5(key + password)  
#
# Then AES-128-CBC or AES-128-ECB of some fixed plaintext

import hashlib, subprocess

def evp_bytes_to_key_md5(password, key_len=16, iv_len=16):
    """OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey with MD5, no salt"""
    data = b""
    d = b""
    while len(data) < key_len + iv_len:
        d = hashlib.md5(d + password).digest()
        data += d
    return data[:key_len], data[key_len:key_len+iv_len]

password = b"test"
key, iv = evp_bytes_to_key_md5(password)
print(f"EVP key for 'test': {key.hex()}")

def aes_encrypt(mode, key_hex, iv_hex, plaintext):
    cmd = ["openssl", "enc", f"-aes-128-{mode}", 
           "-K", key_hex, "-iv", iv_hex, "-nopad", "-nosalt"]

# This likely means:

    print(f"Captain's log encountered an error: \n {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(code)

def generate_cle_bytes(password: str) -> bytes:
    """Generate 18 bytes for .cle file from password"""
    # Use HMAC-SHA256 with a fixed key, take first 18 bytes
    key = b"caps-log-v1-auth"
    return hmac_module.new(key, password.encode('utf-8'), hashlib.sha256).digest()[:18]

def write_cle(log_dir: str, password: str):
    """Write .cle file to log_dir"""
    cle_path = os.path.join(log_dir, CLE_FILENAME)
    cle_bytes = generate_cle_bytes(password)
    with open(cle_path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(cle_bytes)

def read_cle(log_dir: str) -> bytes:
    """Read .cle file from log_dir"""
    cle_path = os.path.join(log_dir, CLE_FILENAME)
    with open(cle_path, 'rb') as f:
        return f.read()

def validate_password(log_dir: str, password: str) -> bool:
    """Validate password against .cle file"""
    try:
        stored = read_cle(log_dir)
        expected = generate_cle_bytes(password)
        return stored == expected
    except:
        return False

def has_cle(log_dir: str) -> bool:
    """Check if .cle file exists"""
    return os.path.exists(os.path.join(log_dir, CLE_FILENAME))

def get_log_filename(log_dir: str, date: datetime.date, fmt: str) -> str:
    """Get the full path for a log file given a date and format"""
    # Format the date according to the format string
    rel_path = date.strftime(fmt)
    return os.path.join(log_dir, rel_path)

def parse_log_filename(filename: str, fmt: str) -> datetime.date:
    """Parse a log filename to get the date. Returns None if doesn't match."""
    try:
        return datetime.datetime.strptime(filename, fmt).date()
    except ValueError:
        return None

def get_all_log_dates(log_dir: str, fmt: str) -> list:
    """Get all log dates from the log directory"""
    dates = []
    # The format may include directory components (e.g., "y%Y/d%Y_%m_%d.md")
    # We need to scan the directory structure
    
    # Extract the directory pattern if any
    dir_part = os.path.dirname(fmt)
    file_part = os.path.basename(fmt)
    
    if dir_part:
        # Has subdirectory - scan all subdirs
        try:
            subdirs = [d for d in os.listdir(log_dir) 
                      if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(log_dir, d))]
        except (OSError, NotADirectoryError):
            return dates
        
        for subdir in subdirs:
            subdir_path = os.path.join(log_dir, subdir)
            try:
                files = os.listdir(subdir_path)
            except OSError:
                continue
            for fname in files:
                if fname.startswith('.'):
                    continue
                rel = os.path.join(subdir, fname)
                date = parse_log_filename(rel, fmt)
                if date:
                    dates.append(date)
    else:
        # Flat directory
        try:
            files = os.listdir(log_dir)
        except OSError:
            return dates
        for fname in files:
            if fname.startswith('.'):
                continue
            date = parse_log_filename(fname, fmt)
            if date:
                dates.append(date)
    
    return sorted(dates)

def parse_log_file(filepath: str, first_line_section: bool = False) -> dict:
    """
    Parse a log file and extract sections and tags.
    Returns dict with 'sections': {section_name: [tags]}, 'root_tags': [tags]
    """
    try:
        with open(filepath, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
    except OSError:
        return {'sections': {}, 'root_tags': []}
    
    sections = {}
    root_tags = []
    current_section = None
    
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        line = line.rstrip('\n')
        
        # Skip first line if not first_line_section
        if i == 0 and not first_line_section:
            continue
        
        # Check for section header (level 1: single #)
        if line.startswith('# ') and not line.startswith('## '):
            section_name = line[2:].strip().lower()
            current_section = section_name
            if current_section not in sections:
                sections[current_section] = []
        elif line.startswith('* '):
            # Tag line
            tag_text = line[2:].strip()
            # Parse tag name (before '(' or ':')
            tag_name = re.split(r'[\s(:]', tag_text)[0].strip().lower()
            if not tag_name:
                continue
            
            if current_section is not None:
                sections[current_section].append(tag_name)
            else:
                root_tags.append(tag_name)
    
    return {'sections': sections, 'root_tags': root_tags}

def collect_all_tags_sections(log_dir: str, fmt: str, year: int, 
                               first_line_section: bool = False) -> tuple:
    """
    Collect all sections and tags from log files for a given year.
    Returns (sections_dict, tags_dict) where keys are names and values are counts.
    """
    dates = get_all_log_dates(log_dir, fmt)
    year_dates = [d for d in dates if d.year == year]
    
    sections_count = {}  # section_name -> count (number of files with this section)
    tags_by_section = {}  # section_name -> {tag_name -> count}
    root_tags_count = {}  # tag_name -> count
    
    for date in year_dates:
        filepath = get_log_filename(log_dir, date, fmt)
        if not os.path.exists(filepath):
            continue
        
        parsed = parse_log_file(filepath, first_line_section)
        
        # Count sections
        for section_name, tags in parsed['sections'].items():
            sections_count[section_name] = sections_count.get(section_name, 0) + 1
            if section_name not in tags_by_section:
                tags_by_section[section_name] = {}
            for tag in tags:
                tags_by_section[section_name][tag] = tags_by_section[section_name].get(tag, 0) + 1
        
        # Count root tags
        for tag in parsed['root_tags']:
            root_tags_count[tag] = root_tags_count.get(tag, 0) + 1
    
    return sections_count, tags_by_section, root_tags_count

def do_encrypt(log_dir: str, password: str):
    """Apply encryption (create .cle file)"""
    print("Applying crypto...")
    
    if has_cle(log_dir):
        error_exit("Already applied")
    
    try:
        write_cle(log_dir, password)
    except OSError as e:
        error_exit(str(e))

def do_decrypt(log_dir: str, password: str):
    """Remove encryption (remove .cle file)"""
    print("Applying crypto...")
    
    if not has_cle(log_dir):
        error_exit("Already applied")
    
    cle_path = os.path.join(log_dir, CLE_FILENAME)
    try:
        os.remove(cle_path)
    except OSError as e:
        error_exit(str(e))

def parse_config(config_path: str) -> dict:
    """Parse INI config file"""
    config = {}
    
    parser = configparser.RawConfigParser()
    try:
        with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
            content = f.read()
        parser.read_string(content)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Failed to open file: {config_path}")
    except Exception:
        pass
    
    # Read top-level options
    if parser.defaults():
        for key, value in parser.defaults().items():
            config[key] = value
    
    for section in parser.sections():
        for key, value in parser.items(section):
            config[f"{section}.{key}"] = value
    
    # Parse boolean fields
    for key in ['sunday-start', 'first-line-section']:
        if key in config:
            config[key] = config[key].lower() in ('true', '1', 'yes')
    
    return config

def open_editor(filepath: str):
    """Open file in $EDITOR"""
    # Create parent directories if needed
    parent = os.path.dirname(filepath)
    if parent:
        os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
    
    editor = os.environ.get('EDITOR', 'vi')
    subprocess.call([editor, filepath])


# TUI Implementation
class CapsLogTUI:
    def __init__(self, stdscr, log_dir: str, log_fmt: str, 
                 sunday_start: bool, first_line_section: bool):
        self.stdscr = stdscr
        self.log_dir = log_dir
        self.log_fmt = log_fmt
        self.sunday_start = sunday_start
        self.first_line_section = first_line_section
        
        self.today = datetime.date.today()
        self.current_year = self.today.year
        self.cursor_date = self.today
        
        # Focus: 0=sections, 1=tags, 2=calendar
        self.focus = 0
        
        # Menu state
        self.selected_section = None  # None = <select none>
        self.selected_tag = None
        self.section_cursor = 0  # 0 = <select none>
        self.tag_cursor = 0
        
        # Scratchpad mode
        self.scratchpad_mode = False
        self.scratchpad_cursor = 0
        self.scratchpads = []
        
        # Load data
        self.refresh_data()
        
        # Initialize colors
        curses.start_color()
        curses.use_default_colors()
        curses.init_pair(1, curses.COLOR_BLUE, -1)   # weekend
        curses.init_pair(2, curses.COLOR_RED, -1)    # today
        curses.init_pair(3, curses.COLOR_YELLOW, -1) # highlighted
        curses.init_pair(4, curses.COLOR_GREEN, -1)  # event
        curses.init_pair(5, -1, -1)                  # normal
        
        curses.curs_set(0)
    
    def refresh_data(self):
        """Reload log data"""
        self.all_dates = get_all_log_dates(self.log_dir, self.log_fmt)
        self.year_dates = [d for d in self.all_dates 
                          if d.year == self.current_year]
        
        # Collect sections and tags
        (self.sections_count, 
         self.tags_by_section, 
         self.root_tags_count) = collect_all_tags_sections(
            self.log_dir, self.log_fmt, self.current_year,
            self.first_line_section
        )
        
        self.sections_list = sorted(self.sections_count.items())
        
        # Build tags list based on selected section
        if self.selected_section is None:
            # Show all tags
            all_tags = {}
            for section_tags in self.tags_by_section.values():
                for tag, count in section_tags.items():
                    all_tags[tag] = all_tags.get(tag, 0) + count
            for tag, count in self.root_tags_count.items():
                all_tags[tag] = all_tags.get(tag, 0) + count
            self.tags_list = sorted(all_tags.items())
        else:
            section_tags = self.tags_by_section.get(self.selected_section, {})
            self.tags_list = sorted(section_tags.items())
        
        # Load scratchpads
        scratch_dir = os.path.join(self.log_dir, SCRATCHPAD_DIR)
        os.makedirs(scratch_dir, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            self.scratchpads = sorted([
                f for f in os.listdir(scratch_dir)
                if not f.startswith('.')
            ])
        except OSError:
            self.scratchpads = []
    
    def get_content_width(self, cols: int) -> tuple:
        """
        Calculate layout sizes based on terminal width.
        Returns (content_width, left_margin, sections_w, tags_w, calendar_w)
        """
        MAX_CONTENT = 144
        content = min(MAX_CONTENT, cols - 1)
        
        if content >= MAX_CONTENT:
            left_margin = (cols - 1 - MAX_CONTENT) // 2
        else:
            left_margin = 0
        
        if content >= 100:
            sections_w = 25
            tags_w = 25
        else:
            # Proportional sizing
            panels = content // 2
            if panels > 50:
                panels = 50
            sections_w = (panels + 1) // 2
            tags_w = panels // 2
        
        calendar_w = content - sections_w - tags_w
        return content, left_margin, sections_w, tags_w, calendar_w
    
    def draw(self):
        """Draw the full TUI"""
        if self.scratchpad_mode:
            self.draw_scratchpad()
            return
        
        self.stdscr.erase()
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        content, left_margin, sections_w, tags_w, calendar_w = self.get_content_width(cols)
        
        # Header line
        year_count = len(self.year_dates)
        header = f"Today is: {self.today.day:02d}. {self.today.month:02d}. {self.today.year}.  | There are {year_count} log entries for year {self.current_year}."
        header_x = left_margin + (content - len(header) + 1) // 2
        if 0 < rows and header_x >= 0:
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(0, header_x, header[:cols - header_x], 
                                   curses.A_BOLD | curses.A_UNDERLINE)
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Calculate layout
        sections_x = left_margin
        tags_x = left_margin + sections_w
        calendar_x = left_margin + sections_w + tags_w
        
        # Draw sections box
        self.draw_sections(1, sections_x, sections_w, rows - 3)
        
        # Draw tags box  
        self.draw_tags(1, tags_x, tags_w, rows - 3)
        
        # Draw calendar box
        self.draw_calendar(1, calendar_x, calendar_w, rows - 3)
        
        # Draw events panel (below sections/tags)
        # (simplified - just show empty events box)
        
        # Draw log preview at bottom
        preview_height = max(3, rows - 33)
        if rows > 33:
            self.draw_preview(rows - preview_height - 1, left_margin, content, preview_height)
        
        # Status bar
        status = "hjkl/arrow keys - navigation | d - delete log | s - see scratchpads | tab - move focus between menus and calendar"
        status_y = rows - 1
        status_x = left_margin + (content - len(status) + 1) // 2
        if status_y < rows and status_x >= 0:
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(status_y, status_x, status[:cols - status_x])
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        self.stdscr.refresh()
    
    def draw_box(self, y, x, width, height, title="", focused=False):
        """Draw a box with optional title"""
        if height < 2 or width < 2:
            return
        
        # Top border
        top = "╭" + title + "─" * (width - 2 - len(title)) + "╮"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y, x, top[:width])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Side borders
        for i in range(1, height - 1):
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(y + i, x, "│")
                self.stdscr.addstr(y + i, x + width - 1, "│")
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Bottom border
        bottom = "╰" + "─" * (width - 2) + "╯"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + height - 1, x, bottom[:width])
        except curses.error:
            pass
    
    def draw_sections(self, y, x, width, height):
        """Draw sections menu"""
        title = "Sections"
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        inner_w = width - 2
        inner_h = height - 2
        
        # Draw box
        self.draw_box(y, x, width, height, title)
        
        # Items: <select none> + sections
        items = [None] + [s[0] for s in self.sections_list]
        
        focused = (self.focus == 0)
        
        for i, item in enumerate(items):
            if i >= inner_h:
                break
            
            item_y = y + 1 + i
            item_x = x + 1
            
            if item is None:
                # <select none>
                count_part = ""
                name = "<select none>"
            else:
                count = self.sections_count.get(item, 0)
                count_part = f"{count:4d} │ "
                # Truncate name to fit
                max_name = inner_w - len(count_part) - 2  # 2 for "> " or "  "
                name = item[:max_name] if len(item) > max_name else item
            
            # Cursor indicator
            is_current = (i == self.section_cursor)
            prefix = "> " if is_current else "  "
            
            if item is None:
                text = f"{prefix}{name}"
            else:
                text = f"{prefix}{count_part}{name}"
            
            # Pad to inner width
            text = text.ljust(inner_w)[:inner_w]
            
            attr = curses.A_NORMAL
            if is_current and focused:
                attr = curses.A_REVERSE
            elif is_current:
                attr = curses.A_BOLD
            
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(item_y, item_x, text[:cols - item_x], attr)
            except curses.error:
                pass
    
    def draw_tags(self, y, x, width, height):
        """Draw tags menu"""
        title = "Tags"
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        inner_w = width - 2
        inner_h = height - 2
        
        # Draw box (dim if not focused)
        focused = (self.focus == 1)
        
        # Top border
        top = "╭" + title + "─" * (width - 2 - len(title)) + "╮"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y, x, top[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Side borders
        for i in range(1, height - 1):
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(y + i, x, "│")
                self.stdscr.addstr(y + i, x + width - 1, "│")
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Bottom border
        bottom = "╰" + "─" * (width - 2) + "╯"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + height - 1, x, bottom[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Items: <select none> + tags
        items = [None] + [t[0] for t in self.tags_list]
        
        for i, item in enumerate(items):
            if i >= inner_h:
                break
            
            item_y = y + 1 + i
            item_x = x + 1
            
            if item is None:
                count_part = ""
                name = "<select none>"
            else:
                count_val = 0
                if self.selected_section is None:
                    # Sum from all sections + root
                    for sec_tags in self.tags_by_section.values():
                        count_val += sec_tags.get(item, 0)
                    count_val += self.root_tags_count.get(item, 0)
                else:
                    count_val = self.tags_by_section.get(self.selected_section, {}).get(item, 0)
                
                count_part = f"{count_val:4d} │ "
                max_name = inner_w - len(count_part) - 2
                name = item[:max_name] if len(item) > max_name else item
            
            is_current = (i == self.tag_cursor)
            prefix = "> " if is_current else "  "
            
            if item is None:
                text = f"{prefix}{name}"
            else:
                text = f"{prefix}{count_part}{name}"
            
            text = text.ljust(inner_w)[:inner_w]
            
            attr = curses.A_NORMAL
            if is_current and focused:
                attr = curses.A_REVERSE
            elif is_current:
                attr = curses.A_BOLD
            
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(item_y, item_x, text[:cols - item_x], attr)
            except curses.error:
                pass
    
    def draw_calendar(self, y, x, width, height):
        """Draw annual calendar"""
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        if width < 2:
            return
        
        inner_w = width - 2
        inner_h = height - 2
        
        # Top border with year title
        title = str(self.current_year)
        top = "╭" + title + "─" * (width - 2 - len(title)) + "╮"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y, x, top[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Right border (just a line down)
        for i in range(1, height - 1):
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(y + i, x + width - 1, "│")
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Bottom border
        bottom = "╰" + "─" * (width - 2) + "╯"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + height - 1, x, bottom[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Draw months
        MONTH_W = 23  # 21 inner + 2 borders
        months_per_row = max(1, inner_w // MONTH_W)
        
        month_y = y + 1
        
        for row in range(3):  # 3 rows of months
            if month_y >= y + height - 1:
                break
            
            months_in_row = min(months_per_row, 12 - row * months_per_row)
            
            if row * months_per_row >= 12:
                break
            
            month_start = row * months_per_row + 1
            month_end = min(12, month_start + months_per_row - 1)
            
            # Calculate height needed for this row of months
            max_weeks = 0
            for m in range(month_start, month_end + 1):
                weeks = self.get_month_weeks(self.current_year, m)
                if weeks > max_weeks:
                    max_weeks = weeks
            
            row_height = max_weeks + 3  # header + day names + weeks + empty row
            
            # Draw month boxes for this row
            for mi, month_num in enumerate(range(month_start, month_end + 1)):
                mx = x + 1 + mi * MONTH_W
                if mx + MONTH_W > x + width:
                    break
                
                month_name = datetime.date(self.current_year, month_num, 1).strftime("%B")
                self.draw_month(month_y, mx, MONTH_W, month_name, month_num, 
                               self.current_year, row_height)
            
            month_y += row_height + 1  # +1 for separator
    
    def get_month_weeks(self, year: int, month: int) -> int:
        """Get number of week rows needed for a month"""
        import calendar
        cal = calendar.monthcalendar(year, month)
        return len(cal)
    
    def draw_month(self, y, x, width, name, month, year, height):
        """Draw a single month calendar"""
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        inner_w = width - 2  # 21
        
        # Top border with month name
        top = "╭" + name + "─" * (inner_w - len(name)) + "╮"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y, x, top[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Day headers
        if self.sunday_start:
            day_header = " S  M  T  W  T  F  S "
        else:
            day_header = " M  T  W  T  F  S  S "
        
        try:
            header_attr = curses.A_UNDERLINE
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + 1, x, "│")
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + 1, x + 1, day_header[:inner_w], header_attr)
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + 1, x + width - 1, "│")
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Draw weeks
        import calendar
        if self.sunday_start:
            cal_weeks = calendar.monthcalendar(year, month)
            # Reorder: Sunday first
            # calendar.monthcalendar uses Monday=0... need Sunday first
            # Python calendar: 0=Mon, 6=Sun by default
            # For Sunday first, shift each week
            new_weeks = []
            for week in cal_weeks:
                # week = [Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun]
                # We want [Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat]
                new_week = [week[6]] + week[:6]
                new_weeks.append(new_week)
            weeks = new_weeks
        else:
            calendar.setfirstweekday(0)  # Monday first
            weeks = calendar.monthcalendar(year, month)
        
        for wi, week in enumerate(weeks):
            week_y = y + 2 + wi
            if week_y >= y + height:
                break
            
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(week_y, x, "│")
                self.stdscr.addstr(week_y, x + width - 1, "│")
            except curses.error:
                pass
            
            week_str = ""
            for di, day in enumerate(week):
                if day == 0:
                    week_str += "   "
                else:
                    d = datetime.date(year, month, day)
                    
                    # Determine color/attribute
                    attr = curses.A_NORMAL
                    
                    if d == self.today:
                        attr = curses.color_pair(2)  # red for today
                    
                    # Check if it's a weekend (Sat=5, Sun=6 in Mon-first)
                    if not self.sunday_start:

        elif key == ord('-'):

                # Handle Feb 29 issues
                self.cursor_date = self.cursor_date.replace(year=self.current_year, day=28)

        elif key == ord('\t'):
            # Cycle focus: sections -> tags -> calendar -> sections
            self.focus = (self.focus + 1) % 3
        elif key == curses.KEY_BTAB:
            # Shift+Tab: cycle backwards
            self.focus = (self.focus - 1) % 3
        elif key in (ord('j'), curses.KEY_DOWN):

        elif key in (ord('k'), curses.KEY_UP):
            self.move_up()
        elif key in (ord('h'), curses.KEY_LEFT):

            self.scratchpad_cursor = max(0, self.scratchpad_cursor - 1)
        elif key == ord('\n') or key == curses.KEY_ENTER:
            if self.scratchpad_cursor == 0:

                self.create_scratchpad()

                scratch_name = self.scratchpads[self.scratchpad_cursor - 1]

                    try:
                        self.stdscr.addstr(input_y, input_x, " " * input_w)

                try:

                    self.stdscr.refresh()
                except curses.error:

        return "".join(chars)

            if i + 1 < len(args):
                i += 1
                config_path = args[i]

        elif arg == '--log-dir-path':
            if i + 1 < len(args):

        elif arg == '--log-name-format':
            if i + 1 < len(args):

        elif arg == '--sunday-start':

        elif arg == '--password':
            if i + 1 < len(args):
                i += 1
                password = args[i]
            else:
                error_exit("option '--password' requires an argument")
        elif arg == '--encrypt':
            do_encrypt_flag = True
        elif arg == '--decrypt':
            do_decrypt_flag = True
        elif arg.startswith('-'):
            error_exit(f"unrecognised option '{arg}'")
        
        i += 1
    
    # Read config file (required unless --help)
    try:
        config = parse_config(config_path)
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        error_exit(str(e))

    if log_dir is None:

            print("Applying crypto...")

        do_decrypt(log_dir, password)

Captain's Log (caps-log) - A CLI journaling tool
Reimplementation in Python

import curses

def error_exit(msg, code=1):
    """Print error message and exit"""
    print(f"Captain's log encountered an error: \n {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(code)

def generate_cle_bytes(password: str) -> bytes:
    """Generate 18 bytes for .cle file from password"""
    # Use HMAC-SHA256 with a fixed key, take first 18 bytes
    key = b"caps-log-v1-auth"
    return hmac_module.new(key, password.encode('utf-8'), hashlib.sha256).digest()[:18]

def write_cle(log_dir: str, password: str):
    """Write .cle file to log_dir"""
    cle_path = os.path.join(log_dir, CLE_FILENAME)
    cle_bytes = generate_cle_bytes(password)
    with open(cle_path, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(cle_bytes)

def read_cle(log_dir: str) -> bytes:
    """Read .cle file from log_dir"""
    cle_path = os.path.join(log_dir, CLE_FILENAME)
    with open(cle_path, 'rb') as f:
        return f.read()

def validate_password(log_dir: str, password: str) -> bool:
    """Validate password against .cle file"""
    try:
        stored = read_cle(log_dir)
        expected = generate_cle_bytes(password)
        return stored == expected
    except:
        return False

def has_cle(log_dir: str) -> bool:
    """Check if .cle file exists"""
    return os.path.exists(os.path.join(log_dir, CLE_FILENAME))

def get_log_filename(log_dir: str, date: datetime.date, fmt: str) -> str:
    """Get the full path for a log file given a date and format"""
    # Format the date according to the format string
    rel_path = date.strftime(fmt)
    return os.path.join(log_dir, rel_path)

def parse_log_filename(filename: str, fmt: str) -> datetime.date:
    """Parse a log filename to get the date. Returns None if doesn't match."""
    try:
        return datetime.datetime.strptime(filename, fmt).date()
    except ValueError:
        return None

def get_all_log_dates(log_dir: str, fmt: str) -> list:
    """Get all log dates from the log directory"""
    dates = []
    # The format may include directory components (e.g., "y%Y/d%Y_%m_%d.md")
    # We need to scan the directory structure

    dir_part = os.path.dirname(fmt)
    file_part = os.path.basename(fmt)
    
    if dir_part:
        # Has subdirectory - scan all subdirs
        try:
            subdirs = [d for d in os.listdir(log_dir) 
                      if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(log_dir, d))]
        except (OSError, NotADirectoryError):
            return dates
        
        for subdir in subdirs:
            subdir_path = os.path.join(log_dir, subdir)
            try:

            if date:
                dates.append(date)
    
    return sorted(dates)

def parse_log_file(filepath: str, first_line_section: bool = False) -> dict:
    """
    Parse a log file and extract sections and tags.
    Returns dict with 'sections': {section_name: [tags]}, 'root_tags': [tags]
    """
    try:
        with open(filepath, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
    except OSError:
        return {'sections': {}, 'root_tags': []}
    
    sections = {}
    root_tags = []
    current_section = None
    
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        line = line.rstrip('\n')
        
        # Skip first line if not first_line_section
        if i == 0 and not first_line_section:
            continue
        
        # Check for section header (level 1: single #)
        if line.startswith('# ') and not line.startswith('## '):
            section_name = line[2:].strip().lower()
            current_section = section_name
            if current_section not in sections:
                sections[current_section] = []
        elif line.startswith('* '):
            # Tag line
            tag_text = line[2:].strip()
            # Parse tag name (before '(' or ':')
            tag_name = re.split(r'[\s(:]', tag_text)[0].strip().lower()
            if not tag_name:
                continue
            
            if current_section is not None:
                sections[current_section].append(tag_name)
            else:
                root_tags.append(tag_name)
    
    return {'sections': sections, 'root_tags': root_tags}

def collect_all_tags_sections(log_dir: str, fmt: str, year: int, 
                               first_line_section: bool = False) -> tuple:
    """
    Collect all sections and tags from log files for a given year.
    Returns (sections_dict, tags_dict) where keys are names and values are counts.
    """
    dates = get_all_log_dates(log_dir, fmt)
    year_dates = [d for d in dates if d.year == year]
    
    sections_count = {}  # section_name -> count (number of files with this section)
    tags_by_section = {}  # section_name -> {tag_name -> count}
    root_tags_count = {}  # tag_name -> count
    
    for date in year_dates:
        filepath = get_log_filename(log_dir, date, fmt)
        if not os.path.exists(filepath):
            continue
        
        parsed = parse_log_file(filepath, first_line_section)
        
        # Count sections
        for section_name, tags in parsed['sections'].items():
            sections_count[section_name] = sections_count.get(section_name, 0) + 1
            if section_name not in tags_by_section:
                tags_by_section[section_name] = {}
            for tag in tags:
                tags_by_section[section_name][tag] = tags_by_section[section_name].get(tag, 0) + 1
        
        # Count root tags
        for tag in parsed['root_tags']:
            root_tags_count[tag] = root_tags_count.get(tag, 0) + 1
    
    return sections_count, tags_by_section, root_tags_count

def do_encrypt(log_dir: str, password: str):
    """Apply encryption (create .cle file)"""
    print("Applying crypto...")
    
    if has_cle(log_dir):
        error_exit("Already applied")
    
    try:
        write_cle(log_dir, password)
    except OSError as e:
        error_exit(str(e))

def do_decrypt(log_dir: str, password: str):
    """Remove encryption (remove .cle file)"""
    print("Applying crypto...")
    
    if not has_cle(log_dir):
        error_exit("Already applied")
    
    cle_path = os.path.join(log_dir, CLE_FILENAME)
    try:
        os.remove(cle_path)
    except OSError as e:
        error_exit(str(e))

def parse_config(config_path: str) -> dict:
    """Parse INI config file"""
    config = {}
    
    parser = configparser.RawConfigParser()
    try:
        with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
            content = f.read()
        parser.read_string(content)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Failed to open file: {config_path}")
    except Exception:
        pass
    
    # Read top-level options
    if parser.defaults():
        for key, value in parser.defaults().items():
            config[key] = value
    
    for section in parser.sections():
        for key, value in parser.items(section):
            config[f"{section}.{key}"] = value
    
    # Parse boolean fields
    for key in ['sunday-start', 'first-line-section']:
        if key in config:
            config[key] = config[key].lower() in ('true', '1', 'yes')
    
    return config

def open_editor(filepath: str):
    """Open file in $EDITOR"""
    # Create parent directories if needed
    parent = os.path.dirname(filepath)
    if parent:
        os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
    
    editor = os.environ.get('EDITOR', 'vi')
    subprocess.call([editor, filepath])


# TUI Implementation
class CapsLogTUI:
    def __init__(self, stdscr, log_dir: str, log_fmt: str, 
                 sunday_start: bool, first_line_section: bool):
        self.stdscr = stdscr
        self.log_dir = log_dir
        self.log_fmt = log_fmt
        self.sunday_start = sunday_start
        self.first_line_section = first_line_section
        
        self.today = datetime.date.today()
        self.current_year = self.today.year
        self.cursor_date = self.today
        
        # Focus: 0=sections, 1=tags, 2=calendar
        self.focus = 0
        
        # Menu state
        self.selected_section = None  # None = <select none>
        self.selected_tag = None
        self.section_cursor = 0  # 0 = <select none>
        self.tag_cursor = 0
        
        # Scratchpad mode
        self.scratchpad_mode = False
        self.scratchpad_cursor = 0
        self.scratchpads = []
        
        # Load data
        self.refresh_data()
        
        # Initialize colors
        curses.start_color()
        curses.use_default_colors()
        curses.init_pair(1, curses.COLOR_BLUE, -1)   # weekend
        curses.init_pair(2, curses.COLOR_RED, -1)    # today
        curses.init_pair(3, curses.COLOR_YELLOW, -1) # highlighted
        curses.init_pair(4, curses.COLOR_GREEN, -1)  # event
        curses.init_pair(5, -1, -1)                  # normal
        
        curses.curs_set(0)
    
    def refresh_data(self):
        """Reload log data"""
        self.all_dates = get_all_log_dates(self.log_dir, self.log_fmt)
        self.year_dates = [d for d in self.all_dates 
                          if d.year == self.current_year]
        
        # Collect sections and tags
        (self.sections_count, 
         self.tags_by_section, 
         self.root_tags_count) = collect_all_tags_sections(
            self.log_dir, self.log_fmt, self.current_year,
            self.first_line_section
        )
        
        self.sections_list = sorted(self.sections_count.items())
        
        # Build tags list based on selected section
        if self.selected_section is None:
            # Show all tags
            all_tags = {}
            for section_tags in self.tags_by_section.values():
                for tag, count in section_tags.items():
                    all_tags[tag] = all_tags.get(tag, 0) + count
            for tag, count in self.root_tags_count.items():
                all_tags[tag] = all_tags.get(tag, 0) + count
            self.tags_list = sorted(all_tags.items())
        else:
            section_tags = self.tags_by_section.get(self.selected_section, {})
            self.tags_list = sorted(section_tags.items())
        
        # Load scratchpads
        scratch_dir = os.path.join(self.log_dir, SCRATCHPAD_DIR)
        os.makedirs(scratch_dir, exist_ok=True)
        try:
            self.scratchpads = sorted([
                f for f in os.listdir(scratch_dir)
                if not f.startswith('.')
            ])
        except OSError:
            self.scratchpads = []
    
    def get_content_width(self, cols: int) -> tuple:
        """
        Calculate layout sizes based on terminal width.
        Returns (content_width, left_margin, sections_w, tags_w, calendar_w)
        """
        MAX_CONTENT = 144
        content = min(MAX_CONTENT, cols - 1)
        
        if content >= MAX_CONTENT:
            left_margin = (cols - 1 - MAX_CONTENT) // 2
        else:
            left_margin = 0
        
        if content >= 100:
            sections_w = 25
            tags_w = 25
        else:
            # Proportional sizing
            panels = content // 2
            if panels > 50:
                panels = 50
            sections_w = (panels + 1) // 2
            tags_w = panels // 2
        
        calendar_w = content - sections_w - tags_w
        return content, left_margin, sections_w, tags_w, calendar_w
    
    def draw(self):
        """Draw the full TUI"""
        if self.scratchpad_mode:
            self.draw_scratchpad()
            return
        
        self.stdscr.erase()
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        content, left_margin, sections_w, tags_w, calendar_w = self.get_content_width(cols)
        
        # Header line
        year_count = len(self.year_dates)
        header = f"Today is: {self.today.day:02d}. {self.today.month:02d}. {self.today.year}.  | There are {year_count} log entries for year {self.current_year}."
        header_x = left_margin + (content - len(header) + 1) // 2
        if 0 < rows and header_x >= 0:
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(0, header_x, header[:cols - header_x], 
                                   curses.A_BOLD | curses.A_UNDERLINE)
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Calculate layout
        sections_x = left_margin
        tags_x = left_margin + sections_w
        calendar_x = left_margin + sections_w + tags_w
        
        # Draw sections box
        self.draw_sections(1, sections_x, sections_w, rows - 3)
        
        # Draw tags box  
        self.draw_tags(1, tags_x, tags_w, rows - 3)
        
        # Draw calendar box
        self.draw_calendar(1, calendar_x, calendar_w, rows - 3)
        
        # Draw events panel (below sections/tags)
        # (simplified - just show empty events box)
        
        # Draw log preview at bottom
        preview_height = max(3, rows - 33)
        if rows > 33:
            self.draw_preview(rows - preview_height - 1, left_margin, content, preview_height)
        
        # Status bar
        status = "hjkl/arrow keys - navigation | d - delete log | s - see scratchpads | tab - move focus between menus and calendar"
        status_y = rows - 1
        status_x = left_margin + (content - len(status) + 1) // 2
        if status_y < rows and status_x >= 0:
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(status_y, status_x, status[:cols - status_x])
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        self.stdscr.refresh()
    
    def draw_box(self, y, x, width, height, title="", focused=False):
        """Draw a box with optional title"""
        if height < 2 or width < 2:
            return
        
        # Top border
        top = "╭" + title + "─" * (width - 2 - len(title)) + "╮"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y, x, top[:width])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Side borders
        for i in range(1, height - 1):
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(y + i, x, "│")
                self.stdscr.addstr(y + i, x + width - 1, "│")
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Bottom border
        bottom = "╰" + "─" * (width - 2) + "╯"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + height - 1, x, bottom[:width])
        except curses.error:
            pass
    
    def draw_sections(self, y, x, width, height):
        """Draw sections menu"""
        title = "Sections"
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        inner_w = width - 2
        inner_h = height - 2
        
        # Draw box
        self.draw_box(y, x, width, height, title)
        
        # Items: <select none> + sections
        items = [None] + [s[0] for s in self.sections_list]
        
        focused = (self.focus == 0)
        
        for i, item in enumerate(items):
            if i >= inner_h:
                break
            
            item_y = y + 1 + i
            item_x = x + 1
            
            if item is None:
                # <select none>
                count_part = ""
                name = "<select none>"
            else:
                count = self.sections_count.get(item, 0)
                count_part = f"{count:4d} │ "
                # Truncate name to fit
                max_name = inner_w - len(count_part) - 2  # 2 for "> " or "  "
                name = item[:max_name] if len(item) > max_name else item
            
            # Cursor indicator
            is_current = (i == self.section_cursor)
            prefix = "> " if is_current else "  "
            
            if item is None:
                text = f"{prefix}{name}"
            else:
                text = f"{prefix}{count_part}{name}"
            
            # Pad to inner width
            text = text.ljust(inner_w)[:inner_w]
            
            attr = curses.A_NORMAL
            if is_current and focused:
                attr = curses.A_REVERSE
            elif is_current:
                attr = curses.A_BOLD
            
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(item_y, item_x, text[:cols - item_x], attr)
            except curses.error:
                pass
    
    def draw_tags(self, y, x, width, height):
        """Draw tags menu"""
        title = "Tags"
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        inner_w = width - 2
        inner_h = height - 2
        
        # Draw box (dim if not focused)
        focused = (self.focus == 1)
        
        # Top border
        top = "╭" + title + "─" * (width - 2 - len(title)) + "╮"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y, x, top[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Side borders
        for i in range(1, height - 1):
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(y + i, x, "│")
                self.stdscr.addstr(y + i, x + width - 1, "│")
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Bottom border
        bottom = "╰" + "─" * (width - 2) + "╯"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + height - 1, x, bottom[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Items: <select none> + tags
        items = [None] + [t[0] for t in self.tags_list]
        
        for i, item in enumerate(items):
            if i >= inner_h:
                break
            
            item_y = y + 1 + i
            item_x = x + 1
            
            if item is None:
                count_part = ""
                name = "<select none>"
            else:
                count_val = 0
                if self.selected_section is None:
                    # Sum from all sections + root
                    for sec_tags in self.tags_by_section.values():
                        count_val += sec_tags.get(item, 0)
                    count_val += self.root_tags_count.get(item, 0)
                else:
                    count_val = self.tags_by_section.get(self.selected_section, {}).get(item, 0)
                
                count_part = f"{count_val:4d} │ "
                max_name = inner_w - len(count_part) - 2
                name = item[:max_name] if len(item) > max_name else item
            
            is_current = (i == self.tag_cursor)
            prefix = "> " if is_current else "  "
            
            if item is None:
                text = f"{prefix}{name}"
            else:
                text = f"{prefix}{count_part}{name}"
            
            text = text.ljust(inner_w)[:inner_w]
            
            attr = curses.A_NORMAL
            if is_current and focused:
                attr = curses.A_REVERSE
            elif is_current:
                attr = curses.A_BOLD
            
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(item_y, item_x, text[:cols - item_x], attr)
            except curses.error:
                pass
    
    def draw_calendar(self, y, x, width, height):
        """Draw annual calendar"""
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        if width < 2:
            return
        
        inner_w = width - 2
        inner_h = height - 2
        
        # Top border with year title
        title = str(self.current_year)
        top = "╭" + title + "─" * (width - 2 - len(title)) + "╮"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y, x, top[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Right border (just a line down)
        for i in range(1, height - 1):
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(y + i, x + width - 1, "│")
            except curses.error:
                pass
        
        # Bottom border
        bottom = "╰" + "─" * (width - 2) + "╯"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + height - 1, x, bottom[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Draw months
        MONTH_W = 23  # 21 inner + 2 borders
        months_per_row = max(1, inner_w // MONTH_W)
        
        month_y = y + 1
        
        for row in range(3):  # 3 rows of months
            if month_y >= y + height - 1:
                break
            
            months_in_row = min(months_per_row, 12 - row * months_per_row)
            
            if row * months_per_row >= 12:
                break
            
            month_start = row * months_per_row + 1
            month_end = min(12, month_start + months_per_row - 1)
            
            # Calculate height needed for this row of months
            max_weeks = 0
            for m in range(month_start, month_end + 1):
                weeks = self.get_month_weeks(self.current_year, m)
                if weeks > max_weeks:
                    max_weeks = weeks
            
            row_height = max_weeks + 3  # header + day names + weeks + empty row
            
            # Draw month boxes for this row
            for mi, month_num in enumerate(range(month_start, month_end + 1)):
                mx = x + 1 + mi * MONTH_W
                if mx + MONTH_W > x + width:
                    break
                
                month_name = datetime.date(self.current_year, month_num, 1).strftime("%B")
                self.draw_month(month_y, mx, MONTH_W, month_name, month_num, 
                               self.current_year, row_height)
            
            month_y += row_height + 1  # +1 for separator
    
    def get_month_weeks(self, year: int, month: int) -> int:
        """Get number of week rows needed for a month"""
        import calendar
        cal = calendar.monthcalendar(year, month)
        return len(cal)
    
    def draw_month(self, y, x, width, name, month, year, height):
        """Draw a single month calendar"""
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        inner_w = width - 2  # 21
        
        # Top border with month name
        top = "╭" + name + "─" * (inner_w - len(name)) + "╮"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y, x, top[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Day headers
        if self.sunday_start:
            day_header = " S  M  T  W  T  F  S "
        else:
            day_header = " M  T  W  T  F  S  S "
        
        try:
            header_attr = curses.A_UNDERLINE
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + 1, x, "│")
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + 1, x + 1, day_header[:inner_w], header_attr)
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + 1, x + width - 1, "│")
        except curses.error:
            pass
        
        # Draw weeks
        import calendar
        if self.sunday_start:
            cal_weeks = calendar.monthcalendar(year, month)
            # Reorder: Sunday first
            # calendar.monthcalendar uses Monday=0... need Sunday first
            # Python calendar: 0=Mon, 6=Sun by default
            # For Sunday first, shift each week
            new_weeks = []
            for week in cal_weeks:
                # week = [Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun]
                # We want [Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat]
                new_week = [week[6]] + week[:6]
                new_weeks.append(new_week)
            weeks = new_weeks
        else:
            calendar.setfirstweekday(0)  # Monday first
            weeks = calendar.monthcalendar(year, month)
        
        for wi, week in enumerate(weeks):
            week_y = y + 2 + wi
            if week_y >= y + height:
                break
            
            try:
                self.stdscr.addstr(week_y, x, "│")
                self.stdscr.addstr(week_y, x + width - 1, "│")
            except curses.error:
                pass
            
            week_str = ""
            for di, day in enumerate(week):
                if day == 0:
                    week_str += "   "
                else:
                    d = datetime.date(year, month, day)
                    
                    # Determine color/attribute
                    attr = curses.A_NORMAL
                    
                    if d == self.today:
                        attr = curses.color_pair(2)  # red for today
                    
                    # Check if it's a weekend (Sat=5, Sun=6 in Mon-first)
                    if not self.sunday_start:
                        is_weekend = (di >= 5)
                    else:
                        is_weekend = (di == 0 or di == 6)
                    
                    if is_weekend and d != self.today:
                        attr = curses.color_pair(1)  # blue for weekend
                    
                    # Check if date has a log entry
                    if d in [date for date in self.all_dates]:
                        attr = curses.A_BOLD
                        if d == self.today:
                            attr |= curses.color_pair(2)
                    
                    # Cursor date
                    if d == self.cursor_date and self.focus == 2:
                        attr = curses.A_REVERSE
                    
                    try:
                        self.stdscr.addstr(week_y, x + 1 + di * 3, 
                                          f"{day:2d}", attr)
                    except curses.error:
                        pass
                    
                    week_str += f"{day:2d} "
            
            # Fill rest of week
            remaining = inner_w - len(week_str)
            if remaining > 0:
                try:
                    self.stdscr.addstr(week_y, x + 1 + len(week) * 3, " " * remaining)
                except curses.error:
                    pass
        
        # Empty row if needed
        for i in range(len(weeks) + 2, height):
            iy = y + i
            if iy < rows:
                try:
                    self.stdscr.addstr(iy, x, "│" + " " * inner_w + "│")
                except curses.error:
                    pass
        
        # Bottom border
        bottom = "╰" + "─" * inner_w + "╯"
        try:
            self.stdscr.addstr(y + height - 1, x, bottom[:cols - x])
        except curses.error:
            pass
    
    def draw_preview(self, y, x, width, height):
        """Draw log entry preview"""
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        title = f"log preview for {self.cursor_date.day:02d}. {self.cursor_date.month:02d}. {str(self.cursor_date.year)[2:]}."

            self.stdscr.addstr(y + 1, title_x, title, curses.A_UNDERLINE | curses.A_BOLD)
        except curses.error:

        # Load and display preview content
        log_path = get_log_filename(self.log_dir, self.cursor_date, self.log_fmt)
        if os.path.exists(log_path):
            try:
                with open(log_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                    content = f.read()
                lines = content.split('\n')

                for i, line in enumerate(lines):
                    if i >= height - 3:

                    disp_line = line[:inner_w]
                    try:
                        self.stdscr.addstr(y + 2 + i, x + 1, disp_line)
                    except curses.error:
                        pass
            except OSError:
                pass
    
    def draw_scratchpad(self):
        """Draw scratchpad manager view"""
        self.stdscr.erase()
        rows, cols = self.stdscr.getmaxyx()
        
        # Title
        title = "Scratchpad Manager"
        tx = (cols - len(title) + 1) // 2
        try:

        elif key == ord('s'):

        elif key == ord('+') or key == ord('='):
            self.current_year += 1
            self.cursor_date = self.cursor_date.replace(year=self.current_year)
            self.refresh_data()
        elif key == ord('-'):
            self.current_year -= 1
            try:
                self.cursor_date = self.cursor_date.replace(year=self.current_year)
            except ValueError:
                # Handle Feb 29 issues
                self.cursor_date = self.cursor_date.replace(year=self.current_year, day=28)
            self.refresh_data()

            # Cycle focus: sections -> tags -> calendar -> sections
            self.focus = (self.focus + 1) % 3
        elif key == curses.KEY_BTAB:
            # Shift+Tab: cycle backwards
            self.focus = (self.focus - 1) % 3

        elif key in (ord('k'), curses.KEY_UP):

        elif key in (ord('h'), curses.KEY_LEFT):

        elif key == ord('\n') or key == curses.KEY_ENTER:

                    self.stdscr.refresh()
